evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mum recalls poignant last words to son missing in Colombia - BBC News Image source, Family photograph Image caption, Nylva McKie-Williams is desperate to hear from her son By Jasmine DuFraisse Published 1 hour ago The mother of a man missing in Colombia for two months has described how his last words to her were: "We will speak at the weekend". Anton Green, brother of ex-Manchester United youth team defender Ro-Shaun Williams, has not been heard from since 6 August. His mum, Nylva McKie-Williams, said it was "so unlike him not to be in contact with us". Footballer Marcus Rashford, who described Anton as a "family friend", recently joined the appeal to help find the 43-year-old. Image source, Family photograph Image caption, Nylva said it is "very strange" not to hear from Anton as he usually keeps in regular contact Anton, who is originally from Whalley Range in Manchester, moved to South America two-and-a-half years ago. Nylva told BBC North West Tonight he kept in weekly contact with his family, but his calls home stopped suddenly at the beginning of August. She said she became concerned when an earthquake struck another part of Colombia a few days after they last spoke. Speaking about their final conversation, his mother said: "We ended the call by saying: 'We will speak at the weekend'." "It just seems very, very strange and it's so unlike him not to be in contact with us." Zak Bolland, 26, smashed the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, where she lived with her young family in Walkden, Salford, on 26 November 2017 as part of an escalating feud, Bolton Coroner's Court heard. Police attended, the windows were boarded up and a statement was taken with Pearson naming Bolland in a statement as the culprit of the attack. Later the same day, he sent Michelle text messages demanding £500 and threatening to petrol bomb her home. Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, were killed when Bolland carried out his threat two weeks later. The inquests were told police had been called to the house for a second time after the text threats. PC Robert Webster, now a detective constable but at the time a probationary officer for Greater Manchester Police, said Michelle was "fed up and frustrated". He said she told him she was an anxious person and unwilling to go to court to prosecute Bolland. 'Extremely busy' The officer said he told her if Bolland denied smashing her windows, it was his word against hers and if she was not prepared to go to court, a conviction was unlikely. Operation Rivercrest targeted homes in and around Heywood, Rochdale. On Wednesday, 16 men aged between 19 and 49, and a 21-year-old woman were arrested on suspicion of offences including drugs supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery, GMP said. After the arrests, the force said the work was carried out to "take the community back" for the people of Heywood. The first raids began on Wednesday began at 05:00 BST, when officers smashed through doors and windows of the homes of people believed to hold senior positions within organised crime. An hour later, a second wave of raids resulted in further arrests. Image source, GMP Image caption, The first round of strikes begun in the early hours of Wednesday morning "This investigation has been six months in the making," said Det Sgt Hannah Taala. She said the plans were formed after an episode of violent disorder back in April. "Due to those arrests, we managed to seize a lot of mobile phones, and then we got a lot of evidence of other criminality," Taala said. She said there has been violence, serious assaults, stabbings, drug offences, and "heaps of theft" in the area since. "They were wreaking havoc, terror, and leaving people frightened, and nobody wants to stop them. "So, it's down to us because we're not scared of them." The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester. Sean Peers, 38, was due to stand trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court earlier but admitted one count of assault by penetration on 15 September 2024. The husband, who has already pleaded guilty to 60 offences against his wife, also admitted a fresh charge of rape and one of sexual assault. Both offences happened last summer. One of the men accused of joining in the abuse, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee in Scotland, has already pleaded guilty to various offences. There are a further 11 men due to stand trial who have denied abusing the same woman between 2018 to November 2025. Peers, from Stockport, was granted conditional bail until sentence, which will take place at the conclusion of the trial involving the other men. The husband, who is no longer part of the trial as a defendant, will also be sentenced at the conclusion of the case and has been remanded in custody. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Five murder arrests after man found dead in Salford - BBC News Image caption, A man in his 40s was found unresponsive in a property on Great Clowes Street in Salford By Dan Wareing North West Published 7 October 2026 Five men have been arrested on suspicion of murder after a man was found dead. A man in his 40s was found unresponsive in a property on Great Clowes Street in the Broughton area of Salford at about 19:50 BST on Tuesday, Greater Manchester said. The man was pronounced dead shortly afterwards. Detectives are urging anyone with information to contact them. The arrested men, aged between 24 and 35, remain in police custody for questioning. Det Ch Insp Ian Partington said: "Our priority is to establish exactly what happened and we are keeping an open mind as we work to build a full picture of the events leading up to his death. "A post-mortem is taking place to establish the cause of death, which will be an important part of our investigation." He said the force was confident "there isn't any wider threat to the public". evidence_packet.evidence_text: Medal of Cheadle Hulme hero killed in last week of WW1 sells for £130k - BBC News Image source, Noonans Image caption, Second lieutenant James Kirk was killed in the last week of World War One By Stewart Whittingham North West Published 1 hour ago A Victoria Cross awarded to a soldier who was killed in the last week of World War One has sold for £130,000. James Kirk, from Cheadle Hulme, died under heavy machine gun fire as he protected soldiers building a bridge in France in November 1918. The 21-year-old second lieutenant carried on fighting even after being shot in the face, having paddled across a canal to single-handedly confront German gunners. His medal was sold by London auctioneers Noonans on 7 October. It had been expected to fetch between £100,000 and £160,000. Noonans said Kirk made "the ultimate sacrifice" as he sought to defend the Royal Engineers who were were trying to bridge the Oise Canal during the Battle of Sambre on 4 November 1918. Kirk took a Lewis machine gun and four magazines and paddled himself across the waterway on a raft made from petrol tins and cork floats "under a most intense machine gun barrage", Noonans said. Image source, Noonans Image caption, James Kirk was awarded the Victoria Cross for his bravery The auctioneers added: "The bank bristled with machine guns. "He set up his Lewis gun at 10 yards range and fired off the whole of his ammunition. "Further ammunition was paddled across to him on the raft and he continued firing, covering the Royal Engineers in their task. "He was wounded in the arm and the face but still fired continuously from a most exposed position until he was shot through the head and fell dead over his gun." Image source, PA Media Image caption, Huge crowds gathered in London to celebrate the end of the war on Arm

The Salford children's home run by Cambian Childcare Ltd went from an "outstanding" rating to "inadequate" in all areas, with Ofsted inspectors finding "the experiences of children and young people are poor and they are not making progress". Problems cited included staff not looking for children when they go missing from home, "not being vigilant" when managing substance misuse risks, and not having full risk assessments and quality control documentation. Cambian Childcare Ltd said since the inspection it has resolved issues raised in the report. One child was moved out of the home "after only living there for a short period of time" due to "an escalation of concerns, with staff unable to keep the child safe", the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. That led to further "distress and instability" for the child, according to the inspector. The recently published report pointed to staffing as a potential cause of the problems. Inspector Michelle Snape said: "Children who have lived in the home have not been cared for by a consistent staff team. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man has pleaded guilty to sexually assaulting a woman who had been drugged and raped by her husband without her knowledge for more than 20 years The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Sean Peers, 38, was due to stand trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court earlier but admitted one count of assault by penetration on 15 September 2024 The husband, who has already pleaded guilty to 60 offences against his wife, also admitted a fresh charge of rape and one of sexual assault. Both offences happened last summer One of the men accused of joining in the abuse, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee in Scotland, has already pleaded guilty to various offences There are a further 11 men due to stand trial who have denied abusing the same woman between 2018 to November 2025

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Victoria Cross awarded to a soldier who was killed in the last week of World War One has sold for £130,000 James Kirk, from Cheadle Hulme, died under heavy machine gun fire as he protected soldiers building a bridge in France in November 1918 The 21-year-old second lieutenant carried on fighting even after being shot in the face, having paddled across a canal to single-handedly confront German gunners His medal was sold by London auctioneers Noonans on 7 October. It had been expected to fetch between £100,000 and £160,000 Noonans said Kirk made "the ultimate sacrifice" as he sought to defend the Royal Engineers who were were trying to bridge the Oise Canal during the Battle of Sambre on 4 November 1918 Kirk took a Lewis machine gun and four magazines and paddled himself across the waterway on a raft made from petrol tins and cork floats "under a most intense machine gun barrage", Noonans said

Eisen Vir Raganit travelled to the woman's Yorkshire home in 2024 The 46-year-old booked an 'experience' on her website, which clearly stated men were required to wear condoms. The woman, a court heard, made it clear Vir Raganit she would only consent to sex if he wore protection Vir Raganit, from Stockport, removed the condom without her knowledge. The practice is known as 'stealthing' Some of the clips were viewed shortly before Vir Raganit met the woman. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Radcliffe The Radcliffe estate where residents' green 'oasis' fears look set to come true Locals believe new school plans are 'entirely the wrong choice' Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:17, 08 Oct 2026 View Image Milton Mea Residents’ fears they could lose an ‘oasis’ at the heart of their estate look set to be realised In the centre of the Milton Road estate, in Radcliffe , sits a green space known locally as Milton Meadows. The space is used by dog walkers, for the annual bonfire night celebrations and as a place for kids to play Over recent years, volunteers have spent ‘hundreds of hours’ transforming the land , clearing it, trimming hedges and planting flowers. The aim was to transform it into an ‘oasis’ in the middle of what has been described as a ‘very depressing estate’ But Bury council confirmed last month it was looking to dispose of the land so a new school could be built there. Despite objections from local residents, the authority’s cabinet is now being asked to approve that sale Documents published by the town hall reveal the school, which would be a pupil referral unit, could cater to 136 children. A pupil referral unit is a non-mainstream setting which can accommodate pupils with additional educational and behavioural needs

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Three arrests in major seven-month investigation into dealing operation Officers also recovered cash, stolen goods and illicit drugs Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 19:28, 07 Oct 2026 View Image A Three men have been arrested as part of a seven-month investigation into a drug dealing network. Officers from Greater Manchester Police and West Midlands Police carried out two raids in Wolverhampton on Wednesday morning (October 7) As well as the arrests, the operation led to the discovery of large quantities of illegal drugs, stolen vehicles and cash The search of an address on Penn Road saw a man in his 60s arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to supply controlled drugs, he remains in police custody. Officers also seized approximately £1,000 in cash and around 50 Class C tablets At the second address on Stephen Close, a teenager was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs and theft of a motor vehicle. A woman in her 40s was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs and child endangerment The pair remain in custody. Police say around 2,000 Class B tablets and a stolen motorcycle were seized at the property, with officers also finding blister packs in a baby’s cot

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Salford mayor calls for city to unite following launch of murder investigation, HMO attack, removal of anti-migrant banners and reports of yobs terrorising suburb 'The spirit of Salford is what unites us' View 6 Images A house on Kingsley Aven Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 18:25, 07 Oct 2026 Updated 20:12, 07 Oct 2026 Salford mayor Paul Dennett has called on the city to unite following 'high-profile incidents... that will have caused concern and anxiety in our communities' Mr Dennett issued a statement after a murder investigation was launched at a property in Lower Broughton ; an 'HMO' was trashed in Kersal ; roadside banners opposing 'migrant HMOs' were put up ; and reports of people being targeted by yobs hurling fireworks amid anti-social behav "Our city motto is 'the welfare of the people is the highest law'," Mr Dennett wrote. "Any attempt to divide people, spread hatred or target individuals because of who they are is completely unacceptable. The spirit of Salford is what unites us." It came as a murder investigation was launched after a man was found dead at a property on Great Clowes Street, Lower Broughton, on Wednesday (October 7). The Manchester Evening News understands the building at the centre of the murder probe is a house of multiple occupancy (HMO) Cops were called following the death of a man in his 40s on Tuesday (October 7). Greater Manchester Police said the man was found unresponsive inside the building

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside Statue of Ricky Hatton will be built in Tameside as council commits to project 'Ricky was a proud son of Tameside whose achievements in boxing and community engagement have inspired many people, young and old, across Tameside and far beyond' A statue will be erected to honour the memory of legendary boxer Ricky Hatton. The 46-year-old was found dead at his home in Hyde in September last year The champion boxer was known across the globe for blockbuster fights against the likes of Floyd Mayweather Jr and Manny Pacquiao. One of his most memorable moments was his brutal stoppage of Kostya Tszyu at the Manchester Arena In the wake of Ricky's death, an online petition to erect a statue in his honour was signed by more than 9,000 people. Now politicians in Tameside are looking to immortalise the fighter by doing just that Allan Hopwood, leader of Reform in the borough, tabled a motion at the latest town hall meeting to get things moving. He called for the statue to be built in Hyde, where he lived, or Hattersley, where he grew up Coun Hopwood said: "Some people in this chamber may already know, but today, October 6, would have been Ricky Hatton's 48th birthday

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Three months after a wanted appeal, he was finally caught Joshua Richards has been jailed Add to preferred sources Comments News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 18:06, 07 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Joshua Richards (Image: GMP) A robber threatened a terrified lone female shop worker with a knife while demanding cash to feed his drug habit Joshua Richards, 25, produced a large kitchen knife and ordered the woman to hand over cash at a convenience store in Stockport . She tried to resist, but handed over £60. Richards fled, after ordering her not to call the police for 10 minutes He was only caught more than three months later after a member of the public identified him from still images circulated from the shop’s CCTV footage. Richards, who at the time of the robbery had no previous convictions and had descended into drug abuse and homelessness, has now Prosecuting, Simon Barrett told Minshull Street Crown Court the shop worker was working at the Go Local Davenport Off Licence on Bramhall Lane, when the defendant entered the shop at about 10.30am on April 1 As he approached the till, he made attempts to cover the bottom half of his face, Mr Barrett said. He then produced a large kitchen knife, and began demanding cash from the till

evidence_packet.summary: Salford Neighbours on Salford street speak of horror as murder investigation launched after man found dead at HMO Five men have been arrested on suspicion of murder Add to preferred sources News Hope Gallagher 17:28, 07 Oct 2026 Updated 17:39, 07 Oct Neighbours of a Salford stree
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Neighbours on Salford street speak of horror as murder investigation launched after man found dead at HMO Five men have been arrested on suspicion of murder Add to preferred sources News Hope Gallagher 17:28, 07 Oct 2026 Updated 17:39, 07 Oct Neighbours of a Salford street have spoken of their horror after a murder investigation was launched after a man was found dead at a HMO Police were called to Great Clowes Street, Lower Broughton, on Wednesday morning (October 7). The Manchester Evening News understands the building at the centre of the murder probe is a house of multiple occupancy (HMO) Cops were called following the death of a man in his 40s on Tuesday (October 7). Greater Manchester Police said the man was found unresponsive inside the building. He sadly died despite the best efforts of emergency services. Five men - aged between 24 and 35 - have been arrested GMP later confirmed the investigation is not being linked to reports of criminal damage at an HMO on nearby Kingsley Avenue , Kersal. Police have twice been called out to the property after it was trashed A witness described a large emergence services presence, with police and air ambulance both in attendance. Another person said roads were 'lined' with ambulances before a large cordon was put in place at around 7.50pm

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Man who had videos about 'stealthing' jailed after raping sex worker Eisen Vir Raganit is behind bars Add to preferred sources News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 16:11, 07 Oct 2026 View Image Eisen Vir Raganit (Image: North Yorksh A man who had videos on his phone about 'stealthing' has been jailed having been convicted of raping a sex worker. Eisen Vir Raganit travelled to the woman's Yorkshire home in 2024 The 46-year-old booked an 'experience' on her website, which clearly stated men were required to wear condoms. The woman, a court heard, made it clear Vir Raganit she would only consent to sex if he wore protection Vir Raganit, from Stockport, removed the condom without her knowledge. The woman challenged him and told him to leave. She later reported the incident to police Vir Raganit's phone was seized by cops. Videos showing men removing condoms during sexual activity without the other person's consent were found. The practice is known as 'stealthing' Some of the clips were viewed shortly before Vir Raganit met the woman. He denied the offence when questioned by police and pleaded guilty when he appeared in court

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Chorlton Manchester mum thought she was 'losing herself' before making one huge decision Georgina Donnelly has started Manchester's Menopause Yoga Club to help other women Add to preferred sources News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 15:21, 0 For millions of women, menopause can arrive with an unnerving collection of symptoms, from sleepless nights and anxiety to brain fog, mood changes and the sudden sense that the body they have known for decades is behaving very differently For one Manchester mum, those changes left her struggling to recognise herself. Her sleep was changing. Her confidence was fading. Her emotions felt unfamiliar and her body no longer felt like her own All the while, life carried on around her. She was still a mum, still dealing with family life and still expected to keep up with the pressures of everyday life Georgina Donnelly, 48, from Chorlton soon recognised that she wasn't on her own, and menopause affected many women in the same way Her own struggle with perimenopause would eventually push her to make a huge decision, turning an experience that had left her feeling alone into a mission to make sure other women did not feel the same

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Dame Sarah Storey says Greater Manchester's public transport is 'still a decade behind London' The region has some catching up to do Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 13:57, 07 Oct 2026 Updated 14:00, 07 Oc A Greater Manchester travel boss has said the region is still ‘a decade or so behind’ the capital when it comes to public transport Dame Sarah Storey, the active travel commissioner for Greater Manchester, told said the region is playing catch-up with London and other European cities when it comes to its reliance on cars over trams, buses, and bikes The Paralympic Games gold medallist and travel policy adviser said: “People here are driving because they feel they don’t have any other choice. It’s the work of the Bee Network to shift that, but change does take time “If I think back to when I was visiting London in preparation for the London 2012 Games, I would never have taken my bike to London. Now I take it every time “We are on that same journey – we’re just a decade or so behind. We’ve got that investment now, and with devolved funding, we can make decisions about local places without having to ask permission all the time.”

Tactical Aid Unit officers smashed through doors and windows from 5am, before arresting people who are believed to hold senior criminal positions Officers arrested 16 men aged between 19 and 49 on suspicion of various offences - including drugs supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery. A 21-year-old woman was also arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of drugs Police seized multiple quantities of drugs, a Surron bike, multiple machetes, knives, and suspected stolen property. A cannabis farm was also found across two floors of a property Detective Sergeant Hannah Taala, from GMP’s Rochdale district, said: "This day has been months in the planning and I am delighted with the results that have already come in. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Mum threatened with petrol bombing not classed by police as vulnerable witness, inquest hears Michelle Pearson received threats from Zak Bolland who smashed her windows with a hammer Add to preferred sources Comments News Greta Simpson Senior A mother of six whose windows were smashed in a ‘tit-for-tat’ feud was not classed by police as an intimidated or vulnerable witness, an inquest has heard Michelle Pearson called police five times in the two weeks leading up to December 11 2017 when her Walken home was petrol-bombed by Zak Bolland and David Worrall, then 23 and 25 Three of Michelle’s children - Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven - died at the scene. Lia, three, passed away from her injuries three days later, while mum Michelle died in hospital twenty months on from the blaze Bolland, 32, and Worrall, 34, were jailed for life and ordered to serve 40 and 37 years respectively after being convicted of the murders of the children in May 2018 Bolland's then girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, then aged 20 and now 29 - who waited in a nearby car while the attack went on - was jailed for 21 years for manslaughter

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford These tattoos could help find family of man found dead in Salford woodland "We have made extensive enquiries to try and identify this man to let his loved ones know however his identity remains known" Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blake Police have shared pictures of tattoos as part of a desperate appeal for help to identify a man who was tragically found dead in woodland in Salford Officers were called to reports of concern for the welfare of a man in the woodland area near Newearth Road in Worsley at around 10.45am on Monday (October 5). Paramedics also raced to the scene, but the sadly the man died A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said there are not believed to be any suspicious circumstances surrounding his death. Following the incident, a file was passed to the coroner and 'extensive checks' were carried out to try and identify the man But his identity 'remains unknown', police said. On Wednesday (October 7) police shared pictures of a number of distinctive tattoos the man had in a bid to identify him and find his loved ones As well as the three pictured, he also had a Scorpio on his left shoulder blade, the initial J on his right arm and a mixture of wording in the middle of his chest. The man is described as a white male of medium build, aged in his mid-30s

The space is used by dog walkers, for the annual bonfire night celebrations and as a place for kids to play Over recent years, volunteers have spent ‘hundreds of hours’ transforming the land , clearing it, trimming hedges and planting flowers. The aim was to transform it into an ‘oasis’ in the middle of what has been described as a ‘very depressing estate’ But Bury council confirmed last month it was looking to dispose of the land so a new school could be built there. Despite objections from local residents, the authority’s cabinet is now being asked to approve that sale Documents published by the town hall reveal the school, which would be a pupil referral unit, could cater to 136 children. title: Three arrests in major seven-month investigation into dealing operation

evidence_packet.title: Three arrests in major seven-month investigation into dealing operation
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Police Three arrests in major seven-month investigation into dealing operation Officers also recovered cash, stolen goods and illicit drugs Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 19:28, 07 Oct 2026 View Image A Three men have been arrested
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police Three arrests in major seven-month investigation into dealing operation Officers also recovered cash, stolen goods and illicit drugs Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 19:28, 07 Oct 2026 View Image A Three men have been arrested
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Three arrests in major seven-month investigation into dealing operation Officers also recovered cash, stolen goods and illicit drugs Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 19:28, 07 Oct 2026 View Image A Three men have been arrested as part of a seven-month investigation into a drug dealing network. Officers from Greater Manchester Police and West Midlands Police carried out two raids in Wolverhampton on Wednesday morning (October 7) As well as the arrests, the operation led to the discovery of large quantities of illegal drugs, stolen vehicles and cash The search of an address on Penn Road saw a man in his 60s arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to supply controlled drugs, he remains in police custody. Officers also seized approximately £1,000 in cash and around 50 Class C tablets At the second address on Stephen Close, a teenager was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs and theft of a motor vehicle. A woman in her 40s was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs and child endangerment The pair remain in custody. Police say around 2,000 Class B tablets and a stolen motorcycle were seized at the property, with officers also finding blister packs in a baby’s cot

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Politics Green Party issues Hannah Spencer statement after 'Zionism is racism' vote The party has spoken out after the controversial motion was passed at the party's conference in Brighton on Sunday Add to preferred sources News Chris Slater Senior Re Gorton and Denton MP Hannah Spencer did not vote in the controversial 'Zionism is racism' motion passed by the Green Party at its conference Members in Brighton on Sunday (October 4) backed the motion, with 1,022 votes in favour and 813 against It declares the Greens to be an 'anti-Zionist party' and sets into its policy that Zionism, the movement to develop and protect a Jewish state in Israel, will be 'treated as any other form of racism' It also supports the establishment of a 'single democratic Palestinian State in all of historic Palestine with Jerusalem as its capital' The party, however, has come under fire for the conference vote, which came just days before the Holborn and St Pancras by-election on Thursday (October 8), in which the Green Party’s leader, Zack Polanski is running

evidence_packet.summary: Salford Salford council tears down 'say no to migrant HMOs' roadside banners amid 'serious misinformation concerns' A Salford councillor said officers were 'surrounded by a gang with dogs and had to leave' when going to remove the banners Add to prefe A council says it will take
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Salford council tears down 'say no to migrant HMOs' roadside banners amid 'serious misinformation concerns' A Salford councillor said officers were 'surrounded by a gang with dogs and had to leave' when going to remove the banners Add to prefe A council says it will take down roadside banners that oppose 'migrant HMOs'. In a statement being shared by councillors, Salford Council said it had 'serious concerns' the banners were 'highly likely to spread misinformation and escalate cohesion issues in communities' The council said it had also acted to 'take steps' to remove them over 'the potential for inciteful behaviour'. The banners - referencing houses of multiple occupation - appeared in areas in Cadishead and Lower Irlam. They have been pictured strung up across lampposts, under brid "Irlam and Cadishead say no to migrant HMOs," read the banners. The council, in a statement issued this week, said: "This matter goes beyond the putting up of union flags, which as a tolerant city have remained in place." The move was welcomed by Cadishead and Lower Irlam councillor Hannah Robinson-Smith, who said in a Facebook post that when highways officers initially attended to remove the flags they were 'surrounded by a gang with dogs, and had to leave' "That is absolutely outrageous," she said. "No-one should be made to feel unsafe undertaking their duties within their employment. These are public infrastructure assets; not a personal exhibition space - no matter the messaging being shared."

Greater Manchester Police said the man was found unresponsive inside the building. He sadly died despite the best efforts of emergency services. Five men - aged between 24 and 35 - have been arrested GMP later confirmed the investigation is not being linked to reports of criminal damage at an HMO on nearby Kingsley Avenue , Kersal. Police have twice been called out to the property after it was trashed A witness described a large emergence services presence, with police and air ambulance both in attendance. Another person said roads were 'lined' with ambulances before a large cordon was put in place at around 7.50pm

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heywood Doors smashed in during dawn raids as 17 arrested as cops swoop on suspected organised crime gang in Heywood Drugs, machetes and suspected stolen property were all recovered by officers Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior repo Seventeen suspects have been arrested in a string of dawn raids as police swoop on an 'organised crime gang'. More than 250 officers stormed the streets of Heywood during two waves of strikes this morning (October 7) Greater Manchester Police says it targeted properties linked to a suspected organised crime group. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Man who had videos about 'stealthing' jailed after raping sex worker Eisen Vir Raganit is behind bars Add to preferred sources News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 16:11, 07 Oct 2026 View Image Eisen Vir Raganit (Image: North Yorksh A man who had videos on his phone about 'stealthing' has been jailed having been convicted of raping a sex worker. Eisen Vir Raganit travelled to the woman's Yorkshire home in 2024 The 46-year-old booked an 'experience' on her website, which clearly stated men were required to wear condoms. The woman, a court heard, made it clear Vir Raganit she would only consent to sex if he wore protection Vir Raganit, from Stockport, removed the condom without her knowledge. The woman challenged him and told him to leave. She later reported the incident to police Vir Raganit's phone was seized by cops. Videos showing men removing condoms during sexual activity without the other person's consent were found. The practice is known as 'stealthing' Some of the clips were viewed shortly before Vir Raganit met the woman. He denied the offence when questioned by police and pleaded guilty when he appeared in court

evidence_packet.lead: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred van

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every morning at 11 almost exactly on the dot, a group of men gather on the ground floor of the Northern Quarter Car Park: that tall, graffiti-coated building on the corner of Church and Tib Street One by one they unlock the padlocks dangling from the back of their flat-tyred vans, and the doors swing open. Out from within comes cart after cart full of corn This is the not-entirely-secret HQ of the Market Street corn vendors: a four-storey council-owned car park, sitting across two of Manchester’s busiest streets. When I get there, the men are working in silence, hands sheathed in black gloves, bags of sweetcorn torn open, cardboard Just as I’m about to approach a vendor, I’m forwarded an email from a reader. It has the subject line The Mystery We All Want Solved "The reason I’m writing is because the people of Manchester are desperate to know what the hell is going on with all of the corn sellers on Market St "Why are there now so many of them? How on earth do they make a profit? Are they independent vendors or all part of the same company? Is their presence legal? What does their proliferation say about the state of the city centre?”

Count Alty’s Fang-tastic Halloween Town Trail will run from Monday October 26 to Sunday November 1, inviting families to hunt for vampires, black cats, bats, ghosts and spiders hidden around the town. Organised by Altrincham BID, the team behind Visit Altrincham, the free trail will see Count Alty arrive in town ahead of his big Halloween party – only to discover that his spooky friends have disappeared. Families can collect a Halloween Trail Sheet from Everyman Altrincham before setting off to find the characters hidden in shop windows and other locations. Some of the characters will also be carrying a special letter, with youngsters challenged to collect them all to reveal a hidden Halloween message. The trail is part of a wider programme of Halloween and half-term events taking place across Altrincham during October. Families can get creative at Halloween Art & Craft at Moge Moge, while Nell’s Pizza will host a Halloween Disco. There are plenty of options for grown-ups too, including a Halloween Bottomless Brunch at Tre Ciccio, Hollywood Halloween at West Beverly and a full Halloween Weekend at House Kitchen & Bar. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Zak Bolland, 26, smashed the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, where she lived with her young family in Walkden, Salford, on 26 November 2017 as part of an escalating feud, Bolton Coroner's Court heard Police attended, the windows were boarded up and a statement was taken with Pearson naming Bolland in a statement as the culprit of the attack Later the same day, he sent Michelle text messages demanding £500 and threatening to petrol bomb her home Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, were killed when Bolland carried out his threat two weeks later The inquests were told police had been called to the house for a second time after the text threats PC Robert Webster, now a detective constable but at the time a probationary officer for Greater Manchester Police, said Michelle was "fed up and frustrated"

evidence_packet.summary: The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Sean Peers, 38, was due to stand trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court earl
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Sean Peers, 38, was due to stand trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court earlier but admitted one count of assault by penetration on 15 September 2024 The husband, who has already pleaded guilty to 60 offences against his wife, also admitted a fresh charge of rape and one of sexual assault. Both offences happened last summer One of the men accused of joining in the abuse, Keith Fotheringham, 59, from Dundee in Scotland, has already pleaded guilty to various offences There are a further 11 men due to stand trial who have denied abusing the same woman between 2018 to November 2025 Peers, from Stockport, was granted conditional bail until sentence, which will take place at the conclusion of the trial involving the other men

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man in his 40s was found unresponsive in a property on Great Clowes Street in the Broughton area of Salford at about 19:50 BST on Tuesday, Greater Manchester said The man was pronounced dead shortly afterwards. Detectives are urging anyone with information to contact them The arrested men, aged between 24 and 35, remain in police custody for questioning Det Ch Insp Ian Partington said: "Our priority is to establish exactly what happened and we are keeping an open mind as we work to build a full picture of the events leading up to his death "A post-mortem is taking place to establish the cause of death, which will be an important part of our investigation." title: Oldham Council agrees interim Lead Member arrangements to strengthen governance and accountability

evidence_packet.title: Oldham Council agrees interim Lead Member arrangements to strengthen governance and accountability
evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Council has approved a new package of interim governance arrangements

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former pub transformed into sheltered accommodation for those struggling with homelessness has been described as a 'blueprint' to be replicated across the country Earlier this year, the former Queens Arms in Newtown was unveiled as a refurbished 14-bed sheltered accommodation, complete with kitchen and washing facilities, to give people in crisis a safe place to stay and receive further support to get back on their feet With homelessness in the national spotlight following Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s pledge to end rough sleeping, it is venues like the Queens Arms and the work of organisations like The Brick and Wigan Council that are being assessed to achieve these aims Councillor Susan Gambles, portfolio holder for housing and welfare, and chair of the homelessness and rough sleeping strategic partnership board, said: “There are some fantastic local partners that work collectively to support people at risk of homelessness, and we are so pleased “What comes across very strongly at their Queens Arms hub is that people are thriving there; they are positive, moving forward, and believing in themselves, and I think that is down to the facilities, the camaraderie, and the staff who care very deeply “This is the template that we should be using across the country, so we will continue championing these services and requesting more funding to be able to do even more like this.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humani Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a stor Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Witches & Healers: Something That Was Ours - Manchester’s Finest Witches & Healers: Something That Was Ours Fri 9th Oct, 2026 - The Portico Library Witches & Healers: Something That Was Ours The Portico Library, 57 Mosley St, Manchester M2 3HY Fri 9th Oct, 2026 Free More info Directions events Go to Manchester's Finest Facebook page Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A new exhibition lands at Portico Library just in time for spooky season. Witches and Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours and explores what it means to be a witch today. Themes explored include wellbeing, aging and place in relation to magic, healing and ritual offering an unparalleled insight into the diverse lives of women who live as witches and healers. Through a feminist lens Hillman uses a mixture of moving image and photography to explore menopause, mental health, outsider identities and sisterhood as well as how women imagine a better world through ritual and magic. Completely free to attend and running until February 2027, drop by to see the exhibition or book in for one of the accompanying workshops or film screenings throughout its run. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян, один из самых ярких представителей современной русскоязычной стендап-сцены, приглашает вас на свой новый сольный концерт. Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Кроме того, он является автором сольных концертов «Жизнь лучший драматург», «Жизнь худший драматург» и «И там, и сям» В новом концерте Гарик с присущими ему наблюдательностью, самоиронией и острым взглядом на происходящее расскажет о жизни, отношениях, эмиграции, повседневных абсурдах и обо всем, что превращает обычные ситуации в блестящую комедию. Не пропустите возможность провести вечер в компании одного из самых самобытных комиков своего поколения. Живой стендап, новые шутки и атмосфера, которую невозможно передать через экран. Хочешь, я приукрашу описание и добавлю несколько фактов? Например, Гарик был пятым участником группы the Beatles, но из-за природной скромности принял решение остаться в тени более пафосных коллег. Так же Гарик писал песни для групп Scorpions и Army of Lovers, является основателем гольф клуба в Майами, пробовал манго. evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

evidence_packet.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
evidence_packet.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

Not vendor keynotes. Not thinly disguised sales pitches. Sessions about the real problems of running and growing a st Merchants first, and everything about the day is built that way. If you run, manage, build or support a store on Magento Open Source or Adobe Commerce, you'll find your people here. Agencies, developers, solution partners and vendors are very welcome too, and the programme is del Two parallel tracks run through the day, mixing merchant case studies, technical deep dives and honest conversations about what's hard. Every talk on the main day is captured and streamed live, so nothing is locked behind being in the room Mage Camp is organised by a consortium of five independent agencies: On Tap, Gene Commerce, PushOn, Foundation Commerce and Monsoon Consulting. No single agency owns it and no one profits from it. It is supported by the Magento Association and Manchester Digital Mage Camp isn't only a date in the calendar. Year-round content for merchants runs on mage.camp from now on, and your ticket connects you to the community beyond the single day

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
